A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 27-page versions of Process Reward Models That Think. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison; the appendices match in both text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original THINKPRM evaluations, including ProcessBench scores, best-of-N selection, guided search, ablations and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations, including Table 2 verification results and the scaling and prompt-sensitivity experiments in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: Synthetic verification-chain generation, process-label filtering, finetuning, solution scoring and parallel/sequential verification procedures are unchanged (Section 3; Appendices A, C and E).

E1.justification: Both versions retain PRM800K training data and the same ProcessBench, MATH-500, AIME ’24, GPQA-Physics and LiveCodeBench evaluation coverage. No task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly mentions LLM-as-a-Judge in v3, but v1 already evaluates it in the corresponding comparisons, including Figures 1 and 8. DiscPRM, majority voting, random baselines and the off-the-shelf PRM comparisons retain their membership.

E3.justification: Evaluation subsets, generators, metrics, sampling budgets, answer-selection rules and beam-search settings remain unchanged (Section 4.1; Appendix E). The added baseline description clarifies an existing setup without reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same training-data scaling, process-versus-outcome filtering, difficulty, verification-compute and prompt-sensitivity analyses, plus failure examples. Figure 12 is relocated without changing its difficulty analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Tables 2–3 retain descriptive invalid-output percentages; these are failure rates rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, curves and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports THINKPRM R1-Qwen-14B F1 scores of 87.3 on OlympiadBench and 85.7 on OmniMath in both versions. Plot styling changes preserve the underlying results.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs are added or revised. Existing mathematical content, including the solution-scoring formula in Appendix E.1 and mathematical examples, is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about data-efficient long-CoT verification, superiority over baseline verifiers, out-of-domain generalization and scaling verification compute.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations are retained, including overconfidence, step-label interference and computational overhead in Section 5.4. Appendix E.7 also retains the qualification that additional math training can reduce out-of-domain performance.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly links the main-experiment LLM-as-a-Judge baseline to the prompting setup in Section 3.1, modestly clarifying an existing experiment. Appendix hyperparameters, hardware, training times, prompt text and promised code/data/model release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning are unchanged. GRACE and Small Language Models Need Strong Verifiers to Self-Correct Reasoning receive publication metadata replacing preprint entries; these are bibliographic updates to the same works.

P1.justification: v3 fixes typos and the malformed Section 5 opening, replaces unhelpful section references with Figures 6–7, and adds a Final Answer Selection paragraph heading. It also updates acknowledgements and bibliographic metadata, while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives revised labels and an expanded caption, Figure 2 changes the LLM-as-a-Judge curve color, and Figures 6–7 receive small sizing adjustments. Figure 12 moves from page 10 to page 11. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 is easier to follow and check because it corrects figure references, cleans up the Section 5 introduction, and clarifies Figure 1 and the baseline setup. These provide a limited documentation and presentation improvement; the scientific evidence, claims and limitations remain unchanged.
